question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the cotangent-cosecant identity 

$$
{csc}^{2}⁡x-1={cot}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic identity

$$
1+{csch}^{2}⁡x={coth}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x+{csch}^{3}⁡x}{\operatorname{coth}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(1+{csch}^{2}⁡x)}{\operatorname{coth}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot {coth}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{coth}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\operatorname{csch}⁡x\,\operatorname{coth}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{csch}⁡x{|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =-(\operatorname{csch}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)-\operatorname{csch}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)) \\  & =\operatorname{csch}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)-\operatorname{csch}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡3) \\  & =\frac{2}{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}-\frac{2}{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡3}} \\  & =\frac{2}{2-{2}^{-1}}-\frac{2}{3-{3}^{-1}} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}-\frac{3}{4} \\  & =\frac{7}{12}\end{aligned}
$$
